title: Butterfly — Goodnotes Test
script: Can Butterfly replace my paid notebook app for this PDF workflow? Five minutes to annotate the same pages: write, highlight, draw a shape, and move a note. I checked organization, responsiveness, and whether the exported PDF kept the marks in place. Sync or collaboration only gets a verdict if I can actually test it on these accounts and devices. [WRITING_ORGANIZATION_AND_EXPORT_RESULTS]. [DEVICE_AND_SYNC_LIMIT]. [SPECIFIC_FIT_AND_GAP]. Would these notes cover what you need?
timingStatus: Estimated silent editorial timings. Refit scenes and caption timestamps to the unchanged voice-over when supplied.
concept: Same PDF: handwriting, shapes, moving notes, export, organization, sync and performance.
whyNow: A practical alternative deserves a current, version-specific check before a viewer changes workflow.
viewerGoal: Decide whether this recorded workflow fits their own devices, plan and needs.
hooks: Can Butterfly replace my paid notebook app for this PDF workflow?
Same PDF, same pen, two note apps.
Would you switch if the exported notes survive?
strongestHook: Can Butterfly replace my paid notebook app for this PDF workflow?
directorBrief: Direct this as a fair matched test with a scoped recommendation: Same PDF: handwriting, shapes, moving notes, export, organization, sync and performance. Keep real app interaction dominant. The final verdict depends on who can use the tool for this recorded workflow, not a universal winner. Capture version, OS and plan so the evidence can be interpreted.
effort: 30–90 minutes capture/test; large transfers and export waiting may add elapsed time.
protocol: Use the same supported device/stylus where possible for Butterfly and Goodnotes; disclose hardware mismatch or inaccessible app. Annotate identical PDF pages for five minutes per tool using fixed text, highlight, rectangle and moved note. Compare readability, object handling, organization, subjective responsiveness and export position. Check sync only with available test devices/accounts; otherwise mark untested. Do not invent latency numbers or universal replacement claims.
evidenceRequirements: Test supported devices; report access gaps and actual limitations.
